title: introduce-latency-penumbra-dashboard-and-contextual-log-rollups
author: Ava Chen
commits: Introduce latency-penumbra dashboard JSON and panels
Add log-rollup worker and compression encoder
Wire rollup config to telemetry pipeline and tests
Fix: null pointer in rollup aggregator when context missing
description: Motivation: We frequently see short-lived tail latency spikes that do not trigger standard SLO alerts but cause persistent customer-facing degradation in streaming responses. Existing dashboards surface p99/p99.9 but lack contextualized log rollups that make those tails actionable without blowing observability cost. Summary: This PR introduces the \"Latency Penumbra\" dashboard and a lightweight contextual log-rollup pipeline that compacts related log fragments into a rollup blob and attaches a small fingerprint to traces so the dashboard can surface summed metrics and representative log excerpts without retrieving full logs on every spike. The change includes: 1) a dashboard (latency_penumbra.jsonnet) with three views: penumbra heatmap (per-route shadow banding around high-percentile latency), cohorted sentinel traces (representative trace thumbnails per spike cluster), and cost delta sparklines (observability cost + token-cost marginal during tail events); 2) a rollup worker that ingests streaming logs and trace anchors, groups short-lived context windows, compresses and deduplicates them, and emits rollup references to traces; 3) an encoder/compressor with lossy-but-safe text delta strategy and a policy-driven retention config to cap cost; 4) query helpers and small API surface to fetch rollup metadata for dashboard drilldowns; 5) docs and runbook that outline triage steps and an automated canary. Implementation notes: The rollup worker is event-driven, written in Go, and uses a modular compressor interface so we can add optimized native implementations later. Rollups are referenced by a short hash attached as trace attribute to avoid rehydrating full logs during routine queries. We tuned grouping windows to 10s by default and added a config knob for noisy routes. Testing: Unit tests for compressor and worker logic, integration test that simulates bursty traffic and validates penumbra heatmap correlation with rollup events, and a CI job to run the dashboard rendering sanity check. Rollout plan: Feature gated via observability.feature.penumbra flag. Start in staging for one week with synthetic replay, then gradual rollout to alpha tenants, then company-wide if telemetry cost growth stays <8%. Backout: toggle the feature flag and delete rollup consumer; rollups are stored with TTL and can be expired. Security and Privacy: rollup compressor strips PII by default using existing redwood scrubber pipeline; customers with strict retention can opt out per-tenant. Migration: No DB schema changes; a small config and index in our time-series store were added. Impact: expected ~25% reduction in exploratory log fetches from dashboard workflows and estimated 7-12% reduction in observability egress costs for alpha tenants. Links: design doc https://linear.app/redwood/board/observability/penumbra-design and runbook snippet in docs/observability/penumbra-playbook.md. Checklist: [x] design reviewed by @DiegoMartinez [x] unit + integration tests [x] docs and runbook [x] staged rollout plan [x] privacy scrubber integration
